title: Denying imputed justification: form of just/holy from new inward righteousness
source_text: XXIX. Similiter quum negant nos per imputatam Christi justitiam justificari, negare non intendunt quin Christi justitia fidelibus donetur atque communicetur, quinque ejus unius & solius merito evadant inferni poenas, peccatis suis alioqui debitas, sed sensus eorum est, Christi meritum & obedientiam non esse formam illam, a qua fideles in Scriptura justi sanctique nominantur, sed istam eorum denominationem a nova justitia sumi, qua intus Spiritus Sancti virtute donati sunt.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise when they deny that we are justified by the imputed righteousness of Christ, they do not intend to deny that Christ's righteousness is given and communicated to the faithful, or that by the merit of it alone they escape the pains of hell otherwise due to their sins, but their sense is that Christ's merit and obedience are not that form from which the faithful in Scripture are named just and holy, but that that denomination of theirs is taken from the new righteousness with which they have been inwardly gifted by the power of the Holy Spirit.
pass_b_english: Romans denying imputed justification still grant Christ's merit frees from hell's pains.
They deny imputation is the form of the name just/holy—that comes from new Spirit-wrought righteousness.
